top_signals.title: 6 Million Barrels in Two Minutes Draws CFTC Scrutiny
top_signals.summary: Oil traders sold futures equivalent to at least 6 million barrels of crude in just two minutes on March 23, shortly before President Donald Trump backed away from threats to strike Iranian power plants. Now, the federal regulator overseeing those trades says it has been looking into the activity. Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Michael Selig said Friday that the agency's enforcement division has been examining oil trading during the Iran war, including the unusual surge preceding Trump's announcement. "Our enforcement division has…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Kenya Records Second Ebola Death as Uganda Restricts Transit
top_signals.summary: Kenya has reported a second death from Ebola, a 65-year-old woman who was a close family member of the index case, while Uganda said it’s restricting transit for anyone with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of the Congo in an effort to halt the disease spreading.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: CMORG holds sector-wide cloud outage simulation exercise
top_signals.summary: The Cross-Market Operational Resilience Group (CMORG) yesterday (8 October 2026) completed its biennial simulation exercise, known as SIMEX26, focused this year on a global cloud services disruption.

top_signals.title: FCC bans two devices with surveillance chips linked to Huawei
top_signals.summary: The banned items — a wireless video transmitter and dashboard camera — are made with chips manufactured by Huawei subsidiary HiSilicon, which markets its products as “designed for the surveillance market.”
